decision: Derive machine edge set by filtering getAdjacencyMap rows through snapshot.can() rather than comparing raw adjacency
alternatives: raw adjacency Set (includes spurious stay self-edges); re-derive edges purely from .can without getAdjacencyMap
reasoning: Spike 6: getAdjacencyMap records a stay self-edge for every state under events that match no guard, so a raw Set has 13 spurious self-loops. Filtering each (state,event) via .can recovers exactly the 21 real edges while still exercising getAdjacencyMap traversal (ac-16)
risk: If a future xstate version changes .can semantics for legal self-loops, the filter could drop the research->research edge; covered by an explicit self-loop assertion
reviewHint: Confirm the .can filter is an acceptable reading of 'getAdjacencyMap edge set equals 21 legal edges'

decision: Placed STEP_TO_STATE_VALUE + stateValueToLeaf in pipeline-machine.ts (exported) and re-exported from fixtures.ts; inlined the single toIs guard in setup rather than creating guards.ts/actions.ts
alternatives: define state-value helpers in fixtures.ts per the plan's file list; create separate guards.ts/actions.ts modules
reasoning: The state-value mapping is structural to the machine and needed by the t4 adapter which precedes t5 fixtures; co-locating avoids duplication (functional-api-reuse) and ordering issues. Only one trivial guard and zero actions exist, so extra files add no value
risk: Reviewer expecting the exact file list may flag the helper relocation; behavior and exhaustiveness are unaffected
